headline: The evening close gets fast without getting thin, tomorrow stops proposing the past, and every count means items.

items.prompt_template: One thing to do once, on each computer you use Command Room from: say "set up command room schedules". This update teaches the background maintenance pass to capture your meetings during the day, so the 5 PM close verifies instead of fetching and lands in minutes — but that instruction lives inside your registered task, which only refreshes when you say the phrase on this machine. Until you do, nothing breaks: the close simply keeps working the old, slower way. Takes seconds, changes nothing else, safe to say more than once.

Tomorrow's plan can no longer contain the past: an item anchored to the day being closed — "tonight", a same-day time, a due date already behind you — is never proposed for the next day. And every due date you see now reads against today: "due Aug 6 — 19 days ago", never a stale "before Thursday".

Your morning brief and evening close now count the way the queues do: items, not fragments. Where several captures are one real piece of work, the headline says so — "9 items, 41 rows" — so the number you see is the number of decisions in front of you.
